saints.name: St. Boniface
saints.title: Bishop and Martyr
saints.shortBlurb: The English monk who became the apostle of Germany, felled the sacred oak of Thor, and died a martyr in Frisia…
biography: Born Wynfreth in Devon about 675 and trained in the monasteries of Exeter and Nursling, he went to Rome in 719, where Pope Gregory II gave him the name Boniface and sent him as missionary bishop to the Germans. Consecrated in 722, he preached in Hesse and Thuringia under the protection of Charles Martel.

At Geismar near Fritzlar he felled the sacred oak of Thor, and when no thunderbolt struck him down, the people asked for baptism; of its wood he built a chapel. Raised to archbishop in 732 and given the see of Mainz in 745, he organized the German Church, reformed the Frankish clergy in synods, and saw his disciple Sturm found the abbey of Fulda.

In old age he resigned his see to finish his first mission among the Frisians. As he waited near Dokkum to confirm a company of converts, a band of heathen robbers fell on the camp and killed him with fifty-two companions on 5 June 754. His body rests at Fulda, and the Apostle of the Germans is honoured as patron of Germany, whose Church he planted.
saints.knownFor: Evangelizing and organizing the Church in Germany.

sources.text: Butler, Lives of the Saints (1866 ed.), 5 June
